Proposition
[$C^0$ estimate for Ricci--DeTurck flow] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0088, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0089, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0090, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0091, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0092 ↗ prop:chow-ii-elementary-parabolic-wmp 1. ch10:10.82\group Ricci-flow applications

For a bounded domain in a complete background with uniformly bounded curvature, the Ricci--DeTurck Dirichlet solution remains uniformly $C^0$-close to the background metric for a time depending only on the desired error, dimension, and curvature bound, independently of the domain.
Proof

\sketch The DeTurck equation has principal part $g^{pq} ar abla _p ar abla _qg_{ij}$. Apply the elementary variant to $\psi =\sum _i\lambda _i^m$, where $\lambda _i$ are the background-relative eigenvalues. The differentiated equation and $g\ge (1-\delta _0) ar g$ make the quadratic gradient terms nonpositive for suitable $m$ and $\delta _0$, leaving $\psi _t\le g^{pq} ar abla _p ar abla _q\psi +A\psi $. The boundary value is $\psi =n$; the variant gives $\psi \le 2n$ for a uniform short time, hence $\lambda _i\le (2n)^{1/m}\le 1+\delta $. The lower bound follows from the preliminary lower estimate, proving the claim.
